content_preview.title: huggingface_hub v2.2.0 Makes hf jobs stats Print One Snapshot by Default and Fixes a Race That Could Let Concurrent Downloads Skip hf_xet
content_preview.summary: The October 8 release changes hf jobs stats to exit after one snapshot unless -f is passed, fixes an hf_xet version-lookup race, and repairs HfFileSystem cache bugs.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

huggingface_hub v2.2.0 was published on October 8, 2026 at 14:54 UTC, according to the [GitHub release page](https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/releases/tag/v2.2.0). The maintainers' notes describe it as "A small release this week, mostly bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements." The most visible change is to the Hugging Face command-line tool: `hf jobs stats` now prints one snapshot and exits instead of streaming metrics until a job finishes. The release also fixes a...

editor_notes.source_verification: Integrity: PR #2596 contains exactly one file (the submission); read from the PR branch via git fetch and git show; title matches; hash_valid and signature_valid true; no stray files; the github-actions verification comment shows 4 sources valid. All four snapshots (source-0..3.html.gz, HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for all) exist and contain real page text (release body, PR descriptions, merged state), not just page chrome. source-0 (release v2.2.0): confirms the quoted 'A small release this week, mostly bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements.'; hf jobs stats used to stream metrics until the job finished, 'scripts and agents calling it on a running job hung until their own timeout'; now prints the latest sample of each job once and exits, like hf jobs logs and hf spaces logs; -f/--follow for the previous live view; --format json|agent|quiet outputs the raw API metrics; HfApi.fetch_job_metrics follow param defaults to False, follow=True streams; both behavior changes listed under Breaking changes (snapshot default; load_torch_model FileNotFoundError and model_index_to_eval_results ValueError on empty list, #5063); race text: 'In a fresh process, the first concurrent hf_hub_download calls could read a placeholder version for hf_xet while another thread was still looking it up. Those calls treated hf_xet as missing and downloaded through the plain HTTP path. This mostly affected parallel downloads such as snapshot_download, where some of the files skipped Xet.'; three HfFileSystem fixes (ls on new empty bucket, replace-not-append listings with duplicates after find()/ls(refresh=True), exists(refresh=True)/invalidate_cache(path) clear cached not-found); Windows glob-expansion fix with the --include "*.json" example; snapshot_download warns on unmatched patterns; hf-xet on Windows ARM64. Release timestamp: the snapshot shows 'released this 08 Oct 14:54' with datetime="2026-10-08T14:54:20Z", and the GitHub API published_at is 2026-10-08T14:54:20Z (not draft, not prerelease), matching the article's 'October 8, 2026 at 14:54 UTC'. source-1 (PR #5090, merged Oct 6): 'Default: one snapshot with the latest sample of each job (~1s). Jobs with no sample within 10s get a warning.'; '-f/--follow ... Only allowed in human mode, since it relies on cursor-up redraws.'; 'Explicit -f rather than switching on TTY or agent detection: whether a command blocks shouldn't depend on where it runs.' All quotes verbatim. source-2 (PR #5102, merged Oct 7): _get_version wrote the placeholder "N/A" into the shared _package_versions cache before importlib.metadata.version; a thread calling is_xet_available() during the lookup took the plain HTTP path, 'so concurrent hf_hub_download calls in a fresh process could skip hf_xet for part of the files'; version now resolved locally and written once; 'Concurrent first calls may each do the lookup, but none of them can read a half-written entry'; new test with 8 threads behind a barrier: 'On main it fails in 10 of 10 runs ... With this change it passes in 20 of 20 runs.' That result is the PR author's own and the article attributes it as such. source-3 (PR #5106, merged Oct 7): invalidate_cache() with no path now also clears the bucket cache; 'Misses stay cached otherwise'. All four sources are github.com first-party project pages (allowlisted).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, quote and flag traces to the cited snapshots. The title wording 'Could Let Concurrent Downloads Skip hf_xet' is not stronger than the sources: PR #5102 says calls 'could skip hf_xet for part of the files' and the release notes say calls 'treated hf_xet as missing and downloaded through the plain HTTP path', which is skipping Xet. The article correctly confines the race to the first concurrent hf_hub_download calls in a fresh process and states that the sources give no figure for how many downloads were affected or how often it occurred. 'Print One Snapshot by Default' matches the release notes and PR #5090. PR merge dates (Oct 6, Oct 7, Oct 7) match the snapshots. Vendor claims are attributed to the release notes and PR authors throughout; the _get_version diagnosis is the PR's own and is attributed to it.
